blocks.text: I can describe weather in spring.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Weather is what the conditions are like in a particular place at a particular time. For example, rain, wind or sun.
Seasons are periods of similar weather. In the UK there are four seasons (spring, summer, autumn and winter).
Spring is the season that comes after winter and before summer.
A rain gauge is a device for measuring how much rain has fallen.
To measure is to find out the size of something or how much of something there is.

blocks.text: The children look at photos from Year 1.
The weather in the photos is not the same.
The weather is often different in each season.
Here are five common types of weather.

items.title: cloudy
items.sub: Lots of clouds in the sky.

blocks.text: Windy weather can be hard to spot.
Look at the trees. Do the branches move?
Cloudy weather does not always mean rain.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Sometimes it is just a cloudy day.

blocks.q: Match each type of weather to its clue.

pairs.b: There are lots of clouds in the sky.
You might see the branches of trees moving.
You will get wet if you go outside.

blocks.text: April is in the season of spring.
Alex visits a farm in April.
The weather changes. Sun. Cloud. Rain.
The weather in spring can be mixed. It can have wind, rain and sunshine at different times.

blocks.q: What can the weather in spring be like?
options: Mixed, with wind, rain and sunshine
blocks.why: Spring weather can be mixed, with periods of wind, rain and sunshine.

blocks.text: Aisha has seen a lot of rain this week.
She thinks tomorrow will be rainy and cloudy too.
When we guess or predict the weather, it is called a {forecast}.

blocks.label: Is a forecast always right?
blocks.text: No. One forecast said rain on Tuesday. It was cloudy.

items.q: What do we call a guess about tomorrow’s weather?
A forecast said rain. It was cloudy. What does this show?
options: A forecast is not always right.

blocks.text: Aisha takes an umbrella when she goes out in spring.
There is often rain in spring.
How can she find out how much rain there is?

blocks.label: Tap to find out
blocks.text: She can use a rain gauge.
A rain gauge collects and measures how much rain has fallen.

items: A rain gauge has numbers on it.
Read the number next to the level of water.
The higher the number, the more rain has fallen.

items.q: One rain gauge shows 10 mm. Another shows 25 mm. Which has more rain?
The rain gauge shows 30 mm on Monday and 10 mm on Tuesday. Which day had more rain?
Where should a rain gauge stay?
options: in your hand while you run

blocks.text: You need a clean plastic bottle, scissors, a ruler or lolly stick, tape and a waterproof pen.

items: An adult cuts the bottle in two.
Turn the top half upside down inside the bottom half. It is a funnel.
Tape a ruler to the side. Zero lines up with the bottom.
Put it outside on a flat surface for 24 hours.
Read the number next to the water.
The weather is often different in each season.
Weather can be cold, cloudy, windy, rainy or sunny.
The weather in spring can be mixed, with wind, rain and sunshine.
Rain can be collected and measured using a rain gauge.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Weather in spring
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short answer.

questions.prompt: Which weather word means “there are lots of clouds in the sky”?
questions.explanation: Cloudy weather means lots of clouds in the sky.

questions.prompt: Which weather word means “you will get wet if you go outside”?
questions.explanation: If you go outside when the weather is rainy, you will get wet.

questions.prompt: Which weather word means “it feels very chilly outside”?
questions.explanation: Cold weather feels very chilly outside.

questions.prompt: Which weather word means “the wind is strong”?
questions.explanation: Windy weather means the wind is strong.

questions.prompt: What do we call a guess or prediction about tomorrow’s weather?
questions.explanation: When we try to guess or predict the weather, it is called a forecast.

questions.prompt: What do we use to collect and measure rain?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures how much rain has fallen.

questions.prompt: Rain gauge A shows 15 mm. Rain gauge B shows 35 mm. Which one has more rain? Write A or B.
questions.explanation: The higher the number, the more rain has fallen, and 35 is higher than 15.
April is in the season of spring.
